CHEMISTRY — TERMLY EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: CHEMISTRY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Industrial manufacture of inorganic chemicals ● Ammonia - The Haber Process. (ra? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Industrial manufacture of inorganic chemicals ● Ammonia - The Haber Process. (ra.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Industrial manufacture of inorganic chemicals ● Ammonia - The Haber Process. (ra.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Industrial manufacture of inorganic chemicals ● Ammonia - The Haber Process. (ra.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Industrial manufacture of inorganic chemicals ● Ammonia - The Haber Process. (ra.

4. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Detergents ● Types of detergents ● Preparation of detergents ● Mode of action of? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Detergents ● Types of detergents ● Preparation of detergents ● Mode of action of.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Detergents ● Types of detergents ● Preparation of detergents ● Mode of action of.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Detergents ● Types of detergents ● Preparation of detergents ● Mode of action of.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Detergents ● Types of detergents ● Preparation of detergents ● Mode of action of.

6. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 0 °C

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrochemistry 2.3 Nuclear chemistry 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Alkanols 3.2 Al? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrochemistry 2.3 Nuclear chemistry 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Alkanols 3.2 Al.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrochemistry 2.3 Nuclear chemistry 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Alkanols 3.2 Al.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Electrochemistry 2.3 Nuclear chemistry 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Alkanols 3.2 Al.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrochemistry 2.3 Nuclear chemistry 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Alkanols 3.2 Al.

8. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Producers

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Carbon and extraction of metals ● Occurrence of carbon (allotropes of carbon-dia? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Carbon and extraction of metals ● Occurrence of carbon (allotropes of carbon-dia.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Carbon and extraction of metals ● Occurrence of carbon (allotropes of carbon-dia.

   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Carbon and extraction of metals ● Occurrence of carbon (allotropes of carbon-dia.

10. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. watt (W)

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Energy Changes in physical and chemical processes ● System and surrounding ● Ene? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Energy Changes in physical and chemical processes ● System and surrounding ● Ene.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Energy Changes in physical and chemical processes ● System and surrounding ● Ene.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Energy Changes in physical and chemical processes ● System and surrounding ● Ene.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Energy Changes in physical and chemical processes ● System and surrounding ● Ene.

   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Detergents 3.4 Polymers Page 12 of 40 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY Strand S.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Detergents 3.4 Polymers Page 12 of 40 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY Strand S.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Detergents 3.4 Polymers Page 12 of 40 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY Strand S.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Detergents 3.4 Polymers Page 12 of 40 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY Strand S.

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Alkanols 3.2 Alkanoic acid 3.3 Detergents 3.4 Polymers Page 12 of 40 1 STRAND 1.? (1 mark)

   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Alkanols 3.2 Alkanoic acid 3.3 Detergents 3.4 Polymers Page 12 of 40 1 STRAND 1..

14. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Only carbon dioxide

15. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nuclear Chemistry ● Stability of isotopes ● Chemical and nuclear reactions ● Rad? (1 mark)
